table_title: What were the five highest-grossing films worldwide in each decade from the 1980s through the 2010s?
db_analog: SELECT decade, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY decade ORDER BY worldwide_gross_usd DESC) AS rank, film, worldwide_gross_usd, release_year FROM films WHERE decade IN ('1980s','1990s','2000s','2010s') QUALIFY rank <= 5 ORDER BY decade, rank
temporal_note: Wikipedia per-decade '[decade]_in_film' articles accessed 2026-04-27. Worldwide gross figures are taken from the 'List of worldwide highest-grossing films' table on each decade page; values reflect lifetime worldwide gross at the time of fetch and may include theatrical re-release earnings (e.g., Avatar's $2.92B includes its 2022 re-release; Titanic's $1.84B includes the 2012 3D and later re-releases). The top-5 ordering itself is stable; the absolute gross values may shift with future re-releases or with Wikipedia table updates.
_extraction_notes: Built by row-binding the top-5 entries from the 'List of worldwide highest-grossing films' table on each of the four Wikipedia '[decade]_in_film' articles for the 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, and 2010s. The 1970s decade is intentionally excluded — its '1970s_in_film' article uses domestic (US+Canada) gross only, with no parallel worldwide table, so including it would force a metric mismatch in a single CSV. Per-decade source pages each use lifetime worldwide gross; this is consistent across all four cited tables. Composite PK is (Decade, Rank). Note that 'The Lion King' appears twice — the 1994 animated original (1990s rank 5) and the 2019 photorealistic remake (2010s rank 5) — these are distinct films sharing a title; the composite PK keeps them as separate rows. Result: 20 rows × 5 columns, 0 duplicate composite PKs.
